artifacts.summary: Verifies the mode-gated section-loading convention against the live skill-literature and skill-distill files: corrected current byte measurements (literature grew to 100,460 B from an 84,265 B stale baseline; distill unchanged at 93,044 B), confirmed fence-interior heading hazard with exact false-positive line numbers, located all eight extraction boundaries, found three cross-references needing repointing, and flagged a Path Selection Rule conflict between the task description and the formalized convention for the distill extraction's destination.

memory_candidates.content: When computing byte sizes for a mode-gated-section-loading extraction candidate in a file with illustrative example-output fences, do not scan for the next line starting with '## ' as the section boundary -- fenced plain-text output examples (e.g. a command's own printed report template) routinely contain lines that look like markdown headings (e.g. '## Literature Status' inside a ``` block demonstrating command output). The correct boundary is the next heading of the SAME semantic kind (e.g. next '## Mode: X' heading), confirmed by tracking fence-open/close state while scanning, or by direct read of the full span before deleting it.

The mode-gated-section-loading convention's Path Selection Rule (extension-owned surface -> that extension's own context subtree, never core's context/formats/) sometimes conflicts with a task description's own informal wording about where an extraction should land. context/formats/ is reserved for cross-cutting agent-system artifact formats (report-format.md, plan-format.md) consumed across task types -- a single skill's single sub-mode output template is domain-specific and belongs in that extension's own context/project/<ext>/ tree instead, even if the task text says 'context/formats/'.
